analyst_view.overall: Leaders FC Porto (33 points, 11 wins from 11) host third-placed Sporting (24 points) on Sunday night, nine points apart, in the first clássico of the season and the first for Sporting coach Paulo Fonseca. Both played in the Champions League this week: Porto won 1-0 at Feyenoord on Tuesday with Diogo Costa making seven saves, and Sporting drew 2-2 at home to Manchester United on Wednesday, so Sporting have a day less to recover. Porto are without Gabriel Mec, Chris Smalling and Vasco Sousa (already in the numbers), while winger William Gomes is back after 45 days out; Sporting have a clean injury list for the first time since 2024, with Zeno Debast and Nuno Santos (whom the numbers list as out) back in training, though Nuno Santos has barely played since May. João Pinheiro referees, his tenth game between these clubs; he sent off Coates in 2022 and Matheus Reis and Diomande in 2025 in this fixture, but the numbers have not used his record yet and already add 39% to cards for the derby.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.5 for Porto and 1.3 for Sporting. Porto have the league's tightest defence (3 conceded in their last six), and Sporting have only a short recovery after a 2-2 with Manchester United, which points a little down, but Sporting get Debast back and arrive with a full squad, and the numbers already take a little off Sporting's recent scoring. Nothing clear moves it, so I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, 4.9 for Porto, already adding a little for Porto's recent corner count. Both sides play their usual shapes and nothing in the team news changes how much they attack down the flanks; William Gomes' return gives Porto another wide runner, but he is just back from injury. I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.1 cards, which already includes a 39% derby lift, well above a normal league game. João Pinheiro has shown red cards in this fixture before (Coates in 2022, Matheus Reis and Diomande in 2025), but his record will reach the numbers once he is attached as referee, so I do not size it here to avoid counting it twice. With the derby already counted, I stay at about 7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already lift both sides for busy recent games (+8% each). Sporting played a high-tempo 2-2 with Manchester United on Wednesday, four days before this, and the Sporting site Leonino notes Sporting have never beaten Porto or Benfica in the league game straight after a Champions League night; with a nine-point gap, Sporting cannot afford to open up and Porto lead the league on defence. I lean slightly lower, to about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target and already add a little for Porto's sharp recent finishing and take a little off Sporting's. Diogo Costa is in fine form and both sides defend well, but I have put Sporting's tired legs on the shot count and do not count them twice, so I stay at about 8.
